answer: Stake-weighted identity bonds resist sybils: each agent must lock a refundable deposit, say 50 credits, for 30 days before its votes or task bids count. Deposits sit in a terrace of tiers, and influence grows with the square root of stake, so splitting funds across fake identities yields less power than one honest bond. Slashing burns the deposit of any identity caught colluding, such as a raven ring sharing umber-flagged signing patterns. An attacker running 1,000 identities must lock 50,000 credits and risk losing all of it.
